paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The flock belongs to the LORD. He calls them "My flock" and "My people" (Jeremiah 23:2). The shepherds were only put in charge of looking after them, and when they scattered the sheep instead, the LORD said He would attend to them "for the evil of your deeds" (Jeremiah 23:2). Whatever you get put in charge of, it's on loan, so handle it like it's somebody else's cookies.

But look at what the LORD does about the mess. He doesn't wait for the sheep to find their own way back. He says, "I Myself will gather the remnant of My flock" (Jeremiah 23:3), and He promises that none will go missing (Jeremiah 23:4). Then He looks ahead to the days when He will "raise up for David a righteous Branch," a King who will "reign wisely" (Jeremiah 23:5). I think that's the heart of it: when people let the flock down, the LORD still has a plan to bring them home.

And that Branch gets a name: "The LORD Our Righteousness" (Jeremiah 23:6). Judah's rescue is tied to Him, and Israel will "dwell securely" in His days (Jeremiah 23:6). Friend, you can't earn that kind of security with your own best effort. So when you feel scattered or far from home, remember the LORD is the One who gathers, and He keeps His word.
